# A subtest reads the enclosing test's clock.
#
# Interpreter-only, and not because of a gap: `t.test()` and `t.tick()` are the
# interpreter's own, and the compiled test agent does not have them. So the
# claim can only be made here.
#
# Given a clock of its own the subtest would start back at Epoch while the
# enclosing test's had already moved, so `t.tick()` advanced one clock and
# `time.now()` read the other -- and across the boundary time appeared to run
# backwards. The subtest's env is a Snapshot and carries the clock already;
# what was missing was the runner's own handle on it.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

component main ui.node {
    var ticks = 0

    time.timer(interval=1s, @tick {
        ticks += 1
    })

    ui.text(value="{ticks}")
}

func testASubtestSharesTheEnclosingClock(t Test, c main) {
    t.tick()

    t.test("inner", func(s Test, c main) {
        // The enclosing test already moved the clock, so a subtest holding one
        // of its own reads an earlier instant than the test that created it.
        var seen time.datetime = time.now()
        s.assert(time.between(time.datetime("2000-01-01T00:00:00"), seen) > 0s)

        // And moving it here has to be visible to the same scope's clock.
        s.tick()
        s.assert(time.between(seen, time.now()) > 0s)
    })
}

ui.window {
    main
}
